notes: Identity assessment: supplied canonical text identifies Firm-Size Wage Gaps, Job Responsibility, and Hierarchical Matching by Jeremy T. Fox, University of Chicago; first page states Journal of Labor Economics, 2009, vol. 27, no. 1, page 83; final printed page is 126; provenance header gives DOI 10.1086/597428 and author-hosted published-paper PDF URL. This is a full primary journal article text, consistent with the assigned reference. No PDF path supplied; no acquisition or rendering performed. Locator is only "p. 31"; treating this as document page 31 leads to journal page 113 (journal pagination starts at 83). There is no printed journal page 31. This page discusses multiple candidate occupational comparisons and employer-size measures, and no description, study identifier, or requested metric resolves the intended test. Candidate evidence only, not assigned values: Table 1 (journal p. 112/document p. 30) distinguishes A blue/white collar: 16,007 unique workers, 359,092 observations; B managers/supervisors/entry-level white collar: 3,413 unique workers, 61,135 observations; C sales managers/salespeople: 2,396 unique workers, 42,234 observations; D engineers/technicians: 1,014 unique workers, 20,474 observations. Counts are reported directly, with repeated worker observations distinct from unique persons; no summation or df inference. Table base sample: male, full-time private-sector employees. Appendix p. 119 further describes removal of imputed labor income, hours, occupation, schooling, industry, union status, and establishment size. Each comparison has establishment and firm size specifications, each reporting 25–100 vs. 1–24 and 100+ vs. 1–24 wage gaps. Printed metric is exp(gl,2 − gl,1) − 1 or exp(gl,3 − gl,1) − 1, as described on p. 111; no conversion performed. Table p-values are tests of equality of the most- versus least-responsible job wage gaps, not p-values for individual wage-gap coefficients. Page 113 gives p < .001 for A, 100+ vs. 1–24 for both employer-size measures, and p < .001 for B establishment-size equality test. For C it describes rejection at all conventional levels. These candidates cannot be assigned to this row from a page locator alone.
